newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. says Merrill wins $875 mln of note sale.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. says Merrill wins $875 mln of note sale.

text.p: New York City on Wednesday said Merrill Lynch and Co Inc was awarded $875 million of the $1.6 billion of revenue anticipation notes that it sold, while five other firms submitted winning bids for the remainder.
"They won $350 million of Series A and $525 million of Series B," said a city official, referring to Merrill Lynch.

The net interest cost for Series A was 3.66 percent. For Series B, the net interest cost was 3.80 percent without the letter of credit and 4.03 percent when its cost was included, said the city official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. After Merrill, the next biggest award was to Painwebber Group Inc, which won a total of $400 million of the notes -- $100 million of Series A and $300 million of Series B. Morgan Stanley Group Inc won a total of $200 million, which was split between the two series of notes.
Bear Stearns Cos Inc was awarded a total of $50 million of the Series B notes.
A joint bid was submitted by Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc and Artemis Capital Group, who won $50 million of Series B.
And Prudential Insurance Co of America's Prudential Securities was awarded $25 million of Series B.
The Series A notes mature on April 15, 1997 and the Series B notes mature on June 30, 1997.

The city, one of the biggest issuers in the municipal market, decided to back the Series B notes with a letter of credit because New York State has a history of failing to approve on time its budget, which is due on April 1.

New York City around the end of the week expects to finalize its plans for a bond sale, which city sources have speculated might run from $750 million to $1 billion, adding it likely would take place around the end of October.
